en: Section B interview.
zh: B节：访谈。

en: In this section you will hear two interviews.
zh: 在这一节中，你将听到两段访谈。

en: At the end of each interview, five questions will be asked about what was said.
zh: 每段访谈结束后，将就刚才所说的内容提出五个问题。

en: Both the interviews and the questions will be spoken once only.
zh: 访谈和问题都只读一遍。

en: After each question, there will be a ten-second pause.
zh: 每个问题之后会有十秒钟的停顿。

en: During the pause, you should read the four choices of A, B, C and D and mark the best answer to each question on Answer Sheet 2.
zh: 请利用停顿时间阅读A、B、C、D四个选项，并在答题卡二上标出每题的最佳答案。

en: You have 30 seconds to preview the choices.
zh: 你有三十秒钟预览选项。

en: Now, listen to the first interview.
zh: 现在请听第一段访谈。

en: Questions 1 to 5 are based on the first interview.
zh: 第1至5题根据第一段访谈提问。

en: Hey, Kathy.
zh: 嘿，凯西。

en: Did you read this article in the magazine?
zh: 你看过杂志上的这篇文章了吗？

en: I can’t believe how much man’s changing the planet.
zh: 我简直不敢相信，人类对地球的改变竟然这么大。

en: Yeah, I had a look at it.
zh: 嗯，我看过了。

en: Quite interesting I suppose if you believe that sort of thing.
zh: 我想，如果你相信这类事情的话，那倒挺有意思。

en: What?
zh: 什么？

en: What do you mean “if you believe that sort of thing?”
zh: 你说“如果你相信这类事情”，是什么意思？

en: Are you saying you don’t believe that we are damaging the planet?
zh: 你是说，你不相信我们正在破坏地球吗？

en: To be honest, Mark, not really.
zh: 说实话，马克，我不太相信。

en: What are you saying?
zh: 你在说什么？

en: Are you saying global warming isn’t a fact?
zh: 你是说，全球变暖不是事实？

en: Deforestation isn’t a fact?
zh: 森林砍伐也不是事实？

en: The greenhouse effect isn’t actually happening?
zh: 温室效应也并没有真的发生？

en: Hey, calm down Mark.
zh: 嘿，马克，冷静一点。

en: I just think too many people take these things as being definitely true without knowing all the facts.
zh: 我只是觉得，有太多人还没了解全部事实，就认定这些事绝对是真的。

en: You really don’t think global warming is happening.
zh: 你真的认为全球变暖并没有发生？

en: You know they’ve said sea levels are going to rise by quite a few meters over the next 50 to 100 years.
zh: 你知道，他们说未来50到100年，海平面将会上升好几米。

en: Weather conditions are getting worse all over the world.
zh: 世界各地的天气状况都在恶化。

en: Can you remember how many big hurricanes there have been in this country over the last few years?
zh: 你还记得过去几年，我们国家遭遇了多少次强飓风吗？

en: I think evidence is all around us.
zh: 我觉得证据就在我们身边。

en: I don’t think we have enough information, to be honest.
zh: 说实话，我认为我们的信息还不够充分。

en: We’ve only been measuring these things for around two or three hundred years.
zh: 我们对这些现象进行测量，不过也就两三百年。

en: We have no idea what was happening 50,000 years ago.
zh: 五万年前发生过什么，我们根本不知道。

en: For all we know, this is just a natural blip, a kind of sudden but temporary change, in the whole climate cycle.
zh: 说不定，这只是整个气候周期中一次自然的小波动，也就是一种突然而短暂的变化。

en: I don’t think we should change how we’re living just because of 20 years of abnormal measurements.
zh: 我不认为，我们仅仅因为二十年的异常测量数据，就应该改变自己的生活方式。

en: And don’t you think all the other effects we’re having on the planet are destructive?
zh: 那么，你不认为我们对地球造成的其他种种影响也具有破坏性吗？

en: What do you mean?
zh: 你指的是什么？

en: I mean like deforestation, overpopulation, threatening the existence of many endangered animals.
zh: 比如森林砍伐、人口过剩，以及威胁许多濒危动物的生存。

en: Pollution of the air and the seas.
zh: 还有对空气和海洋的污染。

en: I mean, I could go on if you want.
zh: 如果你愿意，我还可以继续列举。

en: No, no, I understand what you’re saying.
zh: 不，不，我明白你的意思。

en: And, yes, it’s true that there are several problems worldwide caused by human influence.
zh: 而且，没错，世界各地的确有一些问题是人类活动造成的。

en: I think the destruction of the Amazon rainforest is really dangerous and it’s something we could live to regret.
zh: 我认为，亚马孙雨林遭到破坏确实很危险，将来我们可能会为此后悔。

en: I read somewhere that they were considered to be the lungs of the planet.
zh: 我曾在哪里读到过，它被称为地球之肺。

en: And there we are happily chopping it all down and it would be a shame to lose some of those animals that may become extinct.
zh: 可我们却还高高兴兴地把它砍掉；还有，失去一些可能灭绝的动物也很可惜。

en: You know, like the rhino or the panda.
zh: 比如犀牛或熊猫。

en: But I think we shouldn’t interfere with nature if they are going to become extinct.
zh: 不过我认为，我们不该干涉自然；如果这些动物将要灭绝，

en: Then we have to allow nature to take its course.
zh: 那我们就得让自然顺其发展。

en: You’ve just contradicted yourself in two sentences Kathy.
zh: 凯西，你前后两句话就自相矛盾了。

en: First you said it’s bad that we’re interfering with nature by destroying the rainforest, and then......
zh: 你先说，我们破坏雨林、干涉自然是件坏事，然后又……

en: That’s not the same thing.
zh: 那不是一回事。

en: Well of course it is.
zh: 怎么不是一回事，当然是！

en: The only reason 99% of these animals are endangered is precisely because WE are threatening their habitats either by chopping it down as you say,
zh: 这些动物中99%之所以濒危，恰恰就是因为我们在威胁它们的栖息地：要么像你说的那样砍掉森林，

en: or by expanding towns and farming into areas where these animals normally live and hunt.
zh: 要么把城镇和农田扩展到它们原本生活、觅食的地方。

en: You can’t destroy an animal’s habitat and then turn around and say we can’t interfere with nature to save it.
zh: 你不能先破坏动物的栖息地，然后掉过头来说，不能为了拯救它们而干涉自然。

en: I don’t think having 20 panda cubs in zoos around the world is a very smart way to save an animal.
zh: 我不认为，在世界各地的动物园里养二十只熊猫幼崽，就是拯救一种动物的明智办法。

en: It’s totally artificial and is cruel to the animals involved.
zh: 那完全是人为的，对涉及其中的动物也很残忍。

en: I would go along with that.
zh: 这一点我赞同。

en: Yes.
zh: 是的。

en: The real solution is to save the animals’ original habitat.
zh: 真正的解决办法是保护这些动物原本的栖息地。

en: This is the end of the first interview.
zh: 第一段访谈到此结束。

en: Questions 1 to 5 are based on what you have just heard.
zh: 第1至5题根据你刚才听到的内容提问。

en: Question 1. What do the speakers mainly talk about?
zh: 第1题：两位说话者主要谈论什么？

en: Question 2. What does the woman think of global warming?
zh: 第2题：女士如何看待全球变暖？

en: Question 3. What is the man mainly concerned about?
zh: 第3题：男士主要关心什么？

en: Question 4. What do the speakers both agree about on the topic?
zh: 第4题：在这个话题上，两位说话者都认同什么？

en: Question 5. What is the woman’s attitude toward the topic?
zh: 第5题：女士对这个话题持什么态度？
